--- title: "Teams & scoreboard" --- The ESPN cross-league surface is **uniform**: the same loader name shape works for every league. This guide shows the teams directory and a past-dated scoreboard, each rendered as a real frame at build time. ## Teams — the uniform `espn__teams()` shape ::: {#ecc1f6ea .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import warnings warnings.filterwarnings("ignore") from sportsdataverse.nba import espn_nba_teams from sportsdataverse.nfl import espn_nfl_teams from sportsdataverse.mlb import espn_mlb_teams from sportsdataverse.nhl import espn_nhl_teams nba = espn_nba_teams() print("NBA teams frame:", nba.shape) nba.columns ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` NBA teams frame: (30, 14) ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` ['team_abbreviation', 'team_alternate_color', 'team_color', 'team_display_name', 'team_id', 'team_is_active', 'team_is_all_star', 'team_location', 'team_logos', 'team_name', 'team_nickname', 'team_short_display_name', 'team_slug', 'team_uid'] ``` ::: ::: Every league returns the same tidy column set. Selecting the three columns most readers care about, across four leagues: ::: {#e75de36e .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} import polars as pl frames = { "NBA": espn_nba_teams(), "NFL": espn_nfl_teams(), "MLB": espn_mlb_teams(), "NHL": espn_nhl_teams(), } summary = pl.DataFrame( { "league": list(frames.keys()), "n_teams": [f.height for f in frames.values()], "example_team": [ f.select("team_display_name").row(0)[0] for f in frames.values() ], } ) summary ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: ## Scoreboard — a stable past-dated call Scoreboards take a `dates` argument (`YYYYMMDD`). Using a **past** date keeps the example reproducible — the slate is final and won't change between renders. ::: {#9cd0cfa4 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} from sportsdataverse.mlb import espn_mlb_scoreboard sb = espn_mlb_scoreboard(dates="20240615") # a settled 2024 regular-season date print("scoreboard frame:", sb.shape) sb.columns[:18] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` scoreboard frame: (15, 50) ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ``` ['game_id', 'uid', 'date', 'name', 'short_name', 'season_year', 'season_type', 'season_slug', 'status_type_id', 'status_type_name', 'status_type_state', 'status_type_completed', 'status_type_description', 'status_type_detail', 'status_type_short_detail', 'status_clock', 'status_display_clock', 'status_period'] ``` ::: ::: A few human-readable columns from that slate: ::: {#6d6809d2 .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} keep = [c for c in ["id", "name", "short_name", "status_type_detail"] if c in sb.columns] sb.select(keep).head(8) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=5} ```{=html}
